records.title: Prevent resurrection and dispose late transports
records.decision: Guard both transport publication and connectivity writes against Shutdown. A late successful transport must be closed outside ac.mu, without publishing it or notifying Ready.
records.rationale: Both guards are needed: suppressing a notification alone does not release the returned resource.

records.title: Remove cross-object lock inversion
records.decision: Snapshot cc.conns under cc.mu, release that lock, then reset each addrConn. Never acquire an ac lock while holding cc.mu; current ac-to-cc calls remain ordered. Recheck Shutdown in reset.
records.rationale: A snapshot plus terminal no-op closes the reset/state-update deadlock without making the public API unsafe.

records.title: Honor accepted connections and reset generations
records.decision: A SETTINGS-confirmed successful connection starts the next reconnect attempt without the stale pre-success delay. Explicit reset zeroes the failure history and advances a generation; the upcoming or current backoff wait must observe that generation atomically. A reset before wait registration cannot be lost. Subsequent failed attempts resume normal jittered backoff.
records.rationale: Recomputing a duration alone does not close the channel-generation lost-wakeup window. Success and explicit reset are distinct triggers.

records.title: Require SETTINGS for success-based backoff reset
records.decision: Across On, Hybrid and Off modes, reset failure history only after SETTINGS confirms server acceptance, or on explicit ResetConnectBackoff. Keep Off admission compatibility separately documented.
records.rationale: TCP acceptance is not proof that the server accepted gRPC. This does not silently remove Off mode.

records.title: Parse explicit on as On
records.decision: The literal on selects RequireHandshakeOn, as does the existing default. Off and Hybrid retain their explicit mappings. Cover the actual environment parser in a fresh process.
records.rationale: Tests that directly assign the enum cannot detect the parser defect. The owning component is envconfig.

records.title: Assign IDLE policy to ClientConn
records.decision: Treat idle timeout and channel-level GOAWAY/no-RPC idleness as ClientConn responsibilities. Keep an explicit model link and an unimplemented owning-model work item; do not add addrConn idle timers to satisfy a channel requirement.
records.rationale: Moving the obligation to its actual owner does not claim it is implemented there.

records.title: Allow health recovery over an existing transport
records.decision: Allow TransientFailure_ServerUnhealthy directly to Ready on a valid current-generation SERVING report. No artificial Connecting notification. Document the health extension to the older transition table.
records.rationale: No network reconnection occurred; a synthetic Connecting step would misrepresent the operation.

records.title: Separate missing first health status from stable watches
records.decision: Bound the first valid health response using a configurable first-verdict timeout, defaulting in this evaluation to the existing getMinConnectTimeout() duration. Expiry cancels that health attempt, releases its transport and enters ordinary reconnect/backoff. After a valid SERVING or NOT_SERVING status, silence alone is permitted; no heartbeat timeout or forced reconnect for stable NOT_SERVING. Keep the existing health client retry/backoff for ordinary stream failures. An unexpected terminal helper return while its context is live is a monitoring failure: remove Ready eligibility and restart monitoring with bounded backoff and the first-verdict timeout. UNIMPLEMENTED retains the explicitly documented healthy fallback; canceled or stale generations cannot change the active instance.
records.rationale: The callee retries ordinary stream errors itself. Blindly recycling on each stream error duplicates policy; stable watch silence is not the same as a missing initial verdict. New timeout and unexpected-return behavior are evaluation policy, not a claimed upstream requirement.

records.title: Ignore mutations on a terminal addrConn
records.decision: After Shutdown, resetConnectBackoff is a no-op. tryUpdateAddrs returns true without changing the address list, preserving the wrapper convention that an update to a retired instance does not recreate it. connect continues returning errConnClosing. The wrapper handles an empty address list as teardown; direct empty updates to live instances are rejected without mutation.
records.rationale: Returning false is not sufficient to promise recreation: the wrapper explicitly declines replacement when the old state is Shutdown. Preserve terminality without mutating dead context.

records.title: Remove the unused restart signal
records.decision: Remove tryNextAddrFromStart and its unreachable branches after verifying that no producer fires it. Preserve address-update replacement and its tested restart-from-first-address behavior.
records.rationale: An unproduced signal is not a useful alternate mechanism. Do not introduce in-place restart semantics as cleanup.

records.title: Give local teardown explicit resource ownership
records.decision: Local teardown always cancels its owned dial/backoff/health activity, independently of parent ClientConn cancellation. A canceled backoff worker eventually exits and stops its timer; no fixed completion latency is promised. If a transport exists, detach it under lock; call GracefulClose for errConnDrain and Close for non-drain reasons outside ac.mu. Graceful drain may retain active RPCs; abrupt close terminates them. Late transports follow DR-001.
records.rationale: The transport lifetime is derived from cc.ctx, so the old NAT-5 inference from ac.cancel is invalid. Distinguish graceful drain from abrupt teardown and never call reentrant close callbacks under ac.mu. The current no-transport backoff path already satisfies this contract and is the F-09 slice.

records.title: Scope attempt cleanup to one attempt
records.decision: Restructure per-attempt ownership so its cancel is released on every exit path at the end of that attempt; use an attempt-scoped helper/defer or equivalently proven explicit cleanup. Do not accumulate deferred closures in the long-lived reconnect loop.
records.rationale: A helper with bounded lifetime is easier to audit than deleting the defer while assuming every early return is covered. Active health monitoring retains ownership until that attempt ends.

records.title: Keep explicit resets immediate and document herd risk
records.decision: Do not add hidden jitter to the immediate ResetConnectBackoff API. Retain ordinary backoff jitter; document fleet reset coordination and rate limiting as operator/caller responsibilities.
records.rationale: Changing immediate reset timing would silently change the public promise. No claim that all synchronized retry risk is eliminated.

records.title: Report failure per exhausted address-list pass
records.decision: Use the same per-list-pass TransientFailure policy in all handshake modes. Individual failed addresses remain Connecting while alternatives remain. Document the chosen subchannel-level interpretation and its deviation from a literal per-address reading.
records.rationale: This agrees with the explicit existing multi-address test and avoids mode-dependent output noise.

records.title: Scope ResetConnectBackoff to backoff, not health status
records.decision: Reset the retry history in every live state and wake a real backoff wait. Do not recycle a live transport merely because its health status is NOT_SERVING. Document that immediate reconnection applies to backoff-TF, not health-TF; health recovery follows DR-008.
records.rationale: A health verdict is not a dial-backoff timer. The broad old API prose needs explicit qualification for this substate.

records.title: Retain server-directed keepalive floor with saturation
records.decision: Keep the nondecreasing keepalive floor for the lifetime of its owning ClientConn, with no automatic decay. Double using saturating duration arithmetic capped at the largest representable positive duration; never overflow to a negative or shorter interval. Record this as a ClientConn model obligation.
records.rationale: Accepting the ratchet must not accept integer overflow. The owning object is ClientConn, not addrConn.
